# We are now Cencora. Our shared identity unites us.

Cencora brings the companies and services of AmerisourceBergen together under one new name.

[ Meet Cencora ][86]
[A banner that says We Are Cencora on a pink and purple background]

# Marketplace gives pharmacies access to thousands of uniquely curated front-of-store products

We’re reimagining the procurement process by enabling pharmacies to source all the products they
need from front to back through one convenient platform.
[ Learn more ][87]
[A person viewing the Marketplace homepage on their laptop]

## We are united in our responsibility
## to create healthier futures.

As we pursue our purpose, we make a positive impact on the health of people and animals around the
world.

### Pharmaceutical distribution solutions

Our wholesale and specialty distribution services ensure that crucial medications efficiently,
reliably and securely reach their destinations every day.
[ Learn more ][88]
[AB_1Card_03]

### Manufacturer solutions

In addition to distribution and logistics, we help pharmaceutical manufacturers bring their products
to market – and assist with each step from pre-commercial and clinical trial to broad market
availability and patient adherence.
[ Learn more ][89]
[AB_2_3_Card_03]

### Provider solutions

Our solutions power patient care for pharmacies, physician practices, hospitals and health systems.
[ Learn more ][90]
[AB_2_3_Card_05]

### Animal health solutions

We deliver distribution, technology and innovation for veterinarians, livestock producers and
manufacturers to make a meaningful difference in their businesses and the health of animals.
[ Learn more ][91]
[GettyImages-907614352_JPG]

## In the news

Read the latest press releases and media mentions.
[ Explore newsroom ][92]

## Insights

Access the newest in thought leadership.
[ Explore insights ][93]

# Careers with purpose

With a global presence and 44,000+ team members strong, AmerisourceBergen is committed to making a
difference in the future of health.
[ Explore careers ][94]
[GettyImages-1178

# Building a world of health around every individual

We connect people to the care they need, put medicine and wellness within reach, and drive greater
affordability, simplicity and convenience in everything we do.

## Combining our strengths for you

Health services Health insurance Pharmacy Prescription drug coverage

### Health services

We have an unmatched ability to reach people and provide them with access to the affordable, quality
health care and wellbeing services they need to live their healthiest lives.

[Explore our services ][110]

### Health insurance

Aetna® creates insurance plans that deliver a total, connected, affordable approach to health care.

[Discover Aetna plans ][111]

### Pharmacy

Our neighborhood pharmacies — as well as our prescription delivery and specialty medication services
— are making it as easy as possible for people to get the care they depend on.

[Visit our pharmacy page ][112]

### Prescription drug coverage

Our pharmacy benefit manager, CVS Caremark®, plays a critical role in the health care system by
helping to lower drug costs and expand coverage to the affordable medications people need to stay
healthy.

[Learn about drug coverage ][113]

We connect people to the care they need, put medicine and wellness within reach, and drive greater
affordability, simplicity and convenience in everything we do.

We have an unmatched ability to reach people and provide them with access to the affordable, quality
health care and wellbeing services they need to live their healthiest lives.

### Health insurance

Aetna® creates insurance plans that deliver a total, connected, affordable approach to health care.

### Pharmacy

Our neighborhood pharmacies — as well as our prescription delivery and specialty medication services
— are making it as easy as possible for people to get the care they depend on.

[Visit our pharmacy page ][112]

Our pharmacy benefit manager, CVS Caremark®, plays a critical role in the health care system by
helping to lower drug costs and expand coverage to the affordable medications people need to stay
healthy.

### View transcript

Having 1 kid?...Not exactly simple.

Having 6 kids? Definitely not simple. Wait, that’s 8 people in one family. Whoa.

That means finding ONE tv show they’ll ALL watch.

Making ONE dinner they’ll ALL eat.

And how do you play a board game with 6 kids?…actually, that’s kinda simple.

Okaaay, not so simple.

But it’s not just tantrums.

It’s attitudes.

That’s right. Teenagers.

And how do you decide who gets the last piece of pizza?

But you don’t just have 6 kids, you have 6 kids all with chronic illnesses.

That means on top of it all, you have to manage over 50 prescriptions, medical checkups, and support
everyone’s mental health.

Luckily, you’re not alone…I mean Tricia, obviously YOU’RE not alone.

But you’ve also got CVS Health as your healthcare partner, to manage specialty medications, provide
walk-in appointments, and keep track of it all in the CVS Health app.

So, does that make everything…simple?

No. It makes it simple…er

And sometimes, “simpler” is all you need to live a little happier and healthier.

But who gets the last piece of pizza? That’s still your call.

When you need more than a pharmacy…
CVS Health.
Healthier Happens Together.

 

## Tricia Fitzgerald's Story

Meet the Fitzgerald family: Mom, dad, and 6 kids. Life with chronic conditions is not simple, but
with CVS Health by their side, managing chronic conditions becomes a little… simpler.

And sometimes, “simpler” is all you need to live a little happier and healthier.

But who gets the last piece of pizza? That’s still your call.

When you need more than a pharmacy…
CVS Health.
Healthier Happens Together.

 

## Tricia Fitzgerald's Story

Meet the Fitzgerald family: Mom, dad, and 6 kids. Life with chronic conditions is not simple, but
with CVS Health by their side, managing chronic conditions becomes a little… simpler.

[Learn more][121]

## Happening at CVS Health®

### Here for women

Through our services, products, policies and partnerships, we're supporting the mental and physical
well-being of all women.

[Learn more about women's health][122]

## Investing in America’s health

### Creating a sustainable future

We’re helping shape a better world today, and for generations to come, through our impact
priorities.

[Understand our impact][123]

## Empowering future growth

### Living our purpose

We couldn’t be prouder of our colleagues that have made us the leading health care company.

[Learn more about our people ][124]

### Bring your heart to CVS Health

We are committed to building a workplace where every person is welcome, valued and can fulfill their
potential. Join us! 

[Explore career opportunities][125]

### Vision

We strive to transform Fresenius Kabi in the decade to come. We are committed to increase
efficiencies in the therapy and care of patients and improve access to high-quality healthcare
around the globe.

[healthcare professionals in action]
][107]
[

### Excellence

We are specialized in lifesaving medicines and technologies for critically and chronically ill
patients. With our passion and expertise, we touch the lives of almost 450 million people every
year, each one representing the importance of our work.

[healthcare professionals in action]
][108]

We constantly strive to improve our sustainability footprint. For us, meeting the needs of patients
and healthcare professionals goes hand in hand with responsible and ethical management.

### Vision

We strive to transform Fresenius Kabi in the decade to come. We are committed to increase
efficiencies in the therapy and care of patients and improve access to high-quality healthcare
around the globe.

[healthcare professionals in action]

We are specialized in lifesaving medicines and technologies for critically and chronically ill
patients. With our passion and expertise, we touch the lives of almost 450 million people every
year, each one representing the importance of our work.

[healthcare professionals in action]

We constantly strive to improve our sustainability footprint. For us, meeting the needs of patients
and healthcare professionals goes hand in hand with responsible and ethical management.

the belief that we can fulfill our responsibilities as a corporate citizen by giving back to the
communities we serve. Ever since then, we have pursued the ideal of "doing well by doing good." This

corporate social responsibility program.

spirit of individuals helping society is exemplified through Henry Schein Cares, our global
corporate social responsibility program.

  Business Solutions
  
  Our businesses bring together leading technologies, innovative solutions and hands-on expertise to
  support the entire healthcare ecosystem.
  
  [ Explore ][51]
  All Businesses Listings
  
  Take a look at our list of businesses.
  
  [ Our Businesses ][52]
  * [Pharmaceutical, Medical Supplies & Products Distribution Services][53]
    
    We distribute pharmaceuticals and medical supplies to healthcare settings across North America,
    from pharmacies and hospitals to doctors’ offices and clinics.
    * [Pharmaceutical Distribution Services][54]
    * [Medical Supply Distribution][55]
  * [Pharmacy Services][56]
    
    We help to ensure the financial wellbeing of pharmacies and health systems and support a stable
    work environment for their employees.
  * [Oncology & Multispecialty Solutions][57]
    
    We provide research, insights, technologies and other support to help address challenges in
    cancer and specialty care.
  * [Biopharma Capabilities][58]
    
    We provide a suite of solutions designed to address access, affordability and adherence
    challenges by bridging the gaps between biopharma companies, pharmacies, providers, and payers
    to help patients get on and stay on their medications.
  * [Prescription Benefit Solutions][59]
    
    We offer solutions that enable employers, payers, health-plan brokers and government agencies to
    provide lower-cost options for prescription medications and therapies.
  * [Consumer Products & Services][60]
    
    We help to ensure the financial wellbeing of pharmacies and health systems and support a stable
    work environment for their employees.

# Advancing Health Outcomes for All®

[ Discover McKesson ][125]

## Making Healthcare Happen

McKesson Corporation is a U.S.-based company with approximately 43,000 employees worldwide and
facilities across the U.S. and Canada. We serve as the logistical and operational backbone of the
U.S. healthcare system, helping ensure patients can access the therapies and care they need when and
where they need them.

Business Solutions
 

## Our Areas of Focus

Our services and technology ensure medicines reach every care setting, bring cancer and specialty
care close to home, and help patients break through access and affordability barriers.

We’re reimagining what’s possible by accelerating clinical trials, helping patients start and stay
on therapy, and building a stronger, smarter supply chain for the future.

[ Learn More ][126]

[Person sitting on the floor in a living room, wrapping a bandage around their elbow. A yellow

### [ Consumer Products & Services ][132]

[Worker pulls pallet jack quickly through a warehouse aisle, shelves lined with boxes, motion blur

Strengthening Healthcare
 

## Powering Care Locally

For nearly two centuries, McKesson has strengthened the systems that move care forward by supporting
providers, enabling access to medicines and therapies, and removing barriers across the patient
journey.

  * [Pharmaceutical, Medical Supplies & Products Distribution Services][53]

    from pharmacies and hospitals to doctors’ offices and clinics.

  * [Pharmacy Services][56]
    
    We help to ensure the financial wellbeing of pharmacies and health systems and support a stable
    work environment for their employees.
  * [Oncology & Multispecialty Solutions][57]
    
    We provide research, insights, technologies and other support to help address challenges in
    cancer and specialty care.
  * [Biopharma Capabilities][58]
    
    We provide a suite of solutions designed to address access, affordability and adherence
    challenges by bridging the gaps between biopharma companies, pharmacies, providers, and payers
    to help patients get on and stay on their medications.
  * [Prescription Benefit Solutions][59]
    
    We offer solutions that enable employers, payers, health-plan brokers and government agencies to
    provide lower-cost options for prescription medications and therapies.

# Advancing Health Outcomes for All®

[ Discover McKesson ][125]

## Making Healthcare Happen

McKesson Corporation is a U.S.-based company with approximately 43,000 employees worldwide and
facilities across the U.S. and Canada. We serve as the logistical and operational backbone of the
U.S. healthcare system, helping ensure patients can access the therapies and care they need when and
where they need them.

Business Solutions
 

## Our Areas of Focus

Our services and technology ensure medicines reach every care setting, bring cancer and specialty
care close to home, and help patients break through access and affordability barriers.

We’re reimagining what’s possible by accelerating clinical trials, helping patients start and stay
on therapy, and building a stronger, smarter supply chain for the future.

## Powering Care Locally

For nearly two centuries, McKesson has strengthened the systems that move care forward by supporting
providers, enabling access to medicines and therapies, and removing barriers across the patient
journey.

* ✅ Зарегистрируйтесь и подтвердите e-mail

* Активации и кредиты для боксов, донглов и программ
* Проверка статуса устройств по IMEI/SN

### Как начать работу?
* ✅ Зарегистрируйтесь и подтвердите e-mail
* ✅ Пополните баланс удобным способом в разделе «Пополнить баланс»
* ✅ Выберите услугу и нажмите «Разместить заказ»
* ✅ Ожидайте выполнение заказа – мы работаем быстро и надежно!

### Новости и обновления

Следите за актуальными изменениями и скидками в нашем [Telegram-канале][50].

Управляйте заказами и получайте уведомления через [Telegram-бота][51].

## **Pharmaceutical Manufacturers in India**

**Actiza Pharmaceutical Pvt. Ltd.** is emerging as a leader in pharmaceutical manufacturing,
exporting, and supplying from India.

“Innovate and automate, with human touch in manufacturing process to provide affordable
pharmaceutical products to make a healthier world.”  

Actiza Pharmaceutical Pvt. Ltd. follows high global standards in formulation manufacturing with
latest machinery. We are specialized in the manufacturing and exporting of [finished
formulations][64] that cater to the most demanding global needs. We are on the verge of becoming one
of the largest pharmaceutical companies in India when it comes to [contract manufacturing][65] of
[Tablets][66], [Capsules][67], [Injections][68],[Creams/Ointments][69], [Drops][70], [Infusion][71],
[Inhaler][72], [Lotion][73], [Gel][74], [Suspension / syrup][75], [Nasal Drops/Sprays][76], etc.  

The manufacturing and R&D facility of Actiza Pharmaceutical Pvt. Ltd. is located in Surat, Gujarat,
India. It contains multiple formulation facilities in close proximity that are further sub-divided
to specific zones dedicated to particular tasks. With well-established supply chain and vendor
development systems, we have built an in-house pharmaceutical ecosystem.

Our world-class manufacturing plant is equipped with modern high-speed machines and integrated
packaging lines. Our heavily automated systems include non-fill devices, collators, multi-station
tablet presses, brevetti visual inspection machines, FFS machines and high-speed vial/ampoule
filler/sealer. Our Highly professional research team works hand-in-hand with the machines to
manufacture high-quality cost-efficient products.

To support our end-to-end pharmaceutical capabilities, **[Actiza Industry][77]** operates as a
wholly owned subsidiary of Actiza Pharmaceutical Pvt. Ltd., specializing in the manufacturing of
**Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs)** and **pharmaceutical intermediates**. This backward
integration enhances our ability to maintain strict quality control, optimize supply chains, and
ensure regulatory compliance across all markets. As a reliable **API manufacturer**, Actiza Industry
plays a critical role in delivering high-quality raw materials that power our finished formulations,
reinforcing our commitment to excellence from molecule to medicine.

From dossier preparation to marketing authorization filing, our Pharmaceutical [Regulatory
Services][78] cover CTD, eCTD, and ACTD formats supporting product registration across 40+ countries
in both regulated and semi-regulated markets.

## **These are Some of the Key Features of Our Pharmaceutical Manufacturing Plant:**
* The continuous and uninterrupted flow of Process & Facilities that comply with Schedule “M”
  Specifications & **WHO-GMP **norms.
* Effective sanitation and fully automated HVAC System.
* Facility to manufacture every variety of tablets including un-coated, film-coated, double-layered,
  sugar-coated, enteric coated and slow release tablets.
* VAHP chillers that are 100% environment friendly.
* Duo Pass Reverse Osmosis water system/ de-mineralization plant.
* Multi-Stage Distillation plant.
* De-Humidification unit and dust extraction systems and separate AHUs for each zone.
* Zone-wise segregation of every critical processing activity, to prevent cross-contamination
* Even uniforms are marked with zone-specific colors to ensure complete segregation.
* Isolated and dedicated facilities for producing B-Lactam and Cephalosporin dosage forms.
* Area-specific Air Environment Conditioning with respect to temperature, pressure, humidity,
  filtration, etc.
* Zero-discharge Effluent Treatment Plant.
* Alternative power generation system to ensure uninterrupted production and Separate air handling
  units for each production department.
* In house R&D facility with experienced and talented researchers.

All the above-mentioned facilities are **[WHO, GMP certified and ISO 9001][79]** accredited for
systems. Regular global audits are conducted to further uplift our standards.

As a result, we have grown into leading pharmaceutical drug manufacturers over the years. With the
goodwill and trust of our customers, the best is yet to come!

# Your Global CDMO

As a global CDMO headquartered in Munich, Germany, we are committed to fulfilling the pharmaceutical
needs of clients throughout Europe, Japan and North America. Our approach is rooted in a
customer-centric philosophy that guarantees exceptional quality and service in every aspect.

## [Our Offering][112]

We are a reliable CDMO partner, providing comprehensive Development and Manufacturing services for
drug products, from small molecules to large molecules. We offer end-to-end services for your small
molecule finished dosage forms (FDFs), including sterile and non-sterile liquids, solids, and
semi-solids products, and we are also specialised in biologicals, orphan drugs, clinical trials,
fill-and-finish, and lyophilisation.

[

### Drug Development

][113]

We provide customised **CDMO services **designed to meet the diverse needs of the industry. From
out-licensing and supply to one-off analysis, custom developments, and advanced formulation
services.

[⟶][114]
[

### Commercial Manufacturing

][115]

Our **CDMO manufacturing network** includes four state-of-the-art facilities in Europe and one in
Japan, each staffed with a dedicated team committed to delivering unparalleled quality in every
offering and solution we provide.

[⟶][116]
[

### Clinical Manufacturing

][117]

We guide your project through every phase of clinical manufacturing, from feasibility studies and
pre-clinical material preparation to **GMP-compliant production**. Our end-to-end approach ensures
seamless transitions between phases, delivering high-quality solutions tailored to your clinical
needs. 

[⟶][118]
[

### Our CDMO Services

][119]

We offer fully integrated **CDMO services **covering the entire process: from initial planning and
supply chain management to regulatory affairs, for your drug product.

[⟶][120]

## Our Network

Our global presence as a CDMO spans across seven locations around the world, simplifying
coordination and communication, saving valuable time. This strategic approach allows our clients to
focus on their core competencies.

## Our Network

Our global presence as a CDMO spans across seven locations around the world, simplifying
coordination and communication, saving valuable time. This strategic approach allows our clients to
focus on their core competencies.

[[flag][flag]

### Athens, Greece

With more than 3,000 sqm of R&D facilities, our team in Athens specialises in the development of
Value Added Medicines and has been recently upgraded with HPAPI capabilities.

⟶][121]
[[flag][flag]

### Halden, Norway

Halden is one of the largest and most advanced sterile production facilities in Northern Europe. It
specialises in the production and distribution of IV bags and plastic ampoules using Blow-Fill Seal
(BFS) technology.

⟶][122]
[[flag][flag]

### Jura, Switzerland

We provide a complete range of services tailored to both Clinical Manufacturing and Commercial
Manufacturing needs, and we specialise in small-batch production with a customised approach.  

⟶][123]
[[flag][flag]

### Kawagoe, Japan

Our state-of-the-art manufacturing site specialises in ampoules, tablets and visual inspection
services. We offer excellent customer service in English and Japanese. It has one of the largest
cold storage warehouses in Japan.

⟶][124]
[[flag][flag]

### Livron, France

With over 100 years of experience, Adragos Livron focuses on sterile liquids and suppositories
manufacturing. We handle more than 100 molecules and provide stability studies, narcotics handling
and analytical testing services.

⟶][125]
[[flag][flag]

### Leipzig, Germany

Our manufacturing facility in Leipzig specialises in semi-solid and non-sterile liquid
pharmaceuticals. With over 100 years of experience, we have a track record of providing first-class
service and customer-focused manufacturing.

⟶][126]
[[flag][flag]

### Maisons-Alfort, France

At our facility in France, we manufacture sterile prefilled syringes and liquid or lyophilised
vials.
With high-speed aseptic filling, freeze-drying, and integrated packaging, the site uses
GMP-compliant CIP/SIP and RABS technologies to ensure quality and reliable global supply.

⟶][127]

# Your Global CDMO

As a global CDMO headquartered in Munich, Germany, we are committed to fulfilling the pharmaceutical
needs of clients throughout Europe, Japan and North America. Our approach is rooted in a
customer-centric philosophy that guarantees exceptional quality and service in every aspect.

## [Our Offering][112]

We are a reliable CDMO partner, providing comprehensive Development and Manufacturing services for
drug products, from small molecules to large molecules. We offer end-to-end services for your small
molecule finished dosage forms (FDFs), including sterile and non-sterile liquids, solids, and
semi-solids products, and we are also specialised in biologicals, orphan drugs, clinical trials,
fill-and-finish, and lyophilisation.

[

### Drug Development

][113]

We provide customised **CDMO services **designed to meet the diverse needs of the industry. From
out-licensing and supply to one-off analysis, custom developments, and advanced formulation
services.

[⟶][114]
[

### Commercial Manufacturing

][115]

Our **CDMO manufacturing network** includes four state-of-the-art facilities in Europe and one in
Japan, each staffed with a dedicated team committed to delivering unparalleled quality in every
offering and solution we provide.

[⟶][116]
[

### Clinical Manufacturing

][117]

We guide your project through every phase of clinical manufacturing, from feasibility studies and
pre-clinical material preparation to **GMP-compliant production**. Our end-to-end approach ensures
seamless transitions between phases, delivering high-quality solutions tailored to your clinical
needs. 

[⟶][118]
[

### Our CDMO Services

][119]

We offer fully integrated **CDMO services **covering the entire process: from initial planning and
supply chain management to regulatory affairs, for your drug product.

[⟶][120]

## Our Network

Our global presence as a CDMO spans across seven locations around the world, simplifying
coordination and communication, saving valuable time. This strategic approach allows our clients to
focus on their core competencies.

[[flag][flag]

### Athens, Greece

With more than 3,000 sqm of R&D facilities, our team in Athens specialises in the development of
Value Added Medicines and has been recently upgraded with HPAPI capabilities.

⟶][121]
[[flag][flag]

### Halden, Norway

Halden is one of the largest and most advanced sterile production facilities in Northern Europe. It
specialises in the production and distribution of IV bags and plastic ampoules using Blow-Fill Seal
(BFS) technology.

⟶][122]
[[flag][flag]

### Jura, Switzerland

We provide a complete range of services tailored to both Clinical Manufacturing and Commercial
Manufacturing needs, and we specialise in small-batch production with a customised approach.  

⟶][123]
[[flag][flag]

### Kawagoe, Japan

Our state-of-the-art manufacturing site specialises in ampoules, tablets and visual inspection
services. We offer excellent customer service in English and Japanese. It has one of the largest
cold storage warehouses in Japan.

⟶][124]
[[flag][flag]

### Livron, France

With over 100 years of experience, Adragos Livron focuses on sterile liquids and suppositories
manufacturing. We handle more than 100 molecules and provide stability studies, narcotics handling
and analytical testing services.

⟶][125]
[[flag][flag]

### Leipzig, Germany

Our manufacturing facility in Leipzig specialises in semi-solid and non-sterile liquid
pharmaceuticals. With over 100 years of experience, we have a track record of providing first-class
service and customer-focused manufacturing.

⟶][126]
[[flag][flag]

### Maisons-Alfort, France

At our facility in France, we manufacture sterile prefilled syringes and liquid or lyophilised
vials.
With high-speed aseptic filling, freeze-drying, and integrated packaging, the site uses
GMP-compliant CIP/SIP and RABS technologies to ensure quality and reliable global supply.

⟶][127]

quality, and efficiency. As a preferred partner for leading pharmaceutical and healthcare companies
worldwide, Akums is committed to delivering groundbreaking formulations that meet evolving market
needs.

With 15+ state-of-the-art manufacturing facilities, Akums offers unmatched expertise across diverse
therapeutic segments and dosage forms, including tablets, capsules, injectables, soft gels, syrups,
topicals, nutraceuticals, cosmeceuticals, derma solutions etc. Our robust R&D capabilities drive
innovation, ensuring fast, cost-effective product development that aligns with stringent regulatory
standards.

Akums is also a trusted leader in Active Pharmaceutical Ingredient (API) manufacturing, ensuring a
seamless and high-quality supply of essential raw materials for pharmaceutical formulations. Our API
capabilities are in compliance with international regulatory standards, supporting the development

reinforce our leadership in pharmaceutical manufacturing.

technology transfers, regulatory support, and customized solutions, helping brands expand their

initiatives and energy-efficient manufacturing processes, ensuring responsible business operations

## Akums Drugs and Pharmaceuticals Ltd.: Leading the Way in Pharma Manufacturing

▼

Akums Drugs & Pharmaceuticals Ltd. stands as India’s largest and most trusted Contract Development
and Manufacturing Organization (CDMO), redefining pharmaceutical excellence through innovation,
quality, and efficiency. As a preferred partner for leading pharmaceutical and healthcare companies
worldwide, Akums is committed to delivering groundbreaking formulations that meet evolving market
needs.

With 15+ state-of-the-art manufacturing facilities, Akums offers unmatched expertise across diverse
therapeutic segments and dosage forms, including tablets, capsules, injectables, soft gels, syrups,
topicals, nutraceuticals, cosmeceuticals, derma solutions etc. Our robust R&D capabilities drive
innovation, ensuring fast, cost-effective product development that aligns with stringent regulatory
standards.

Akums is also a trusted leader in Active Pharmaceutical Ingredient (API) manufacturing, ensuring a
seamless and high-quality supply of essential raw materials for pharmaceutical formulations. Our API
capabilities are in compliance with international regulatory standards, supporting the development
of superior formulations while enhancing supply chain reliability for our partners.

Quality at Akums is more than a benchmark—it is a culture. We adhere to global regulatory standards,
including WHO-GMP, USFDA, EU-GMP, and TGA, ensuring that every product meets the highest safety and
efficacy standards. Our advanced Quality Management System (QMS) and compliance-driven approach
reinforce our leadership in pharmaceutical manufacturing.

Akums collaborates with 1500+ pharmaceutical companies, manufacturing over 4100+ commercialized
formulations. Our expertise extends beyond manufacturing to include formulation development,
technology transfers, regulatory support, and customized solutions, helping brands expand their
portfolios and market presence seamlessly.

While innovation fuels our growth, sustainability shapes our future. Akums integrates eco-friendly
initiatives and energy-efficient manufacturing processes, ensuring responsible business operations
that contribute to a healthier planet.

Leading the Make in India initiative, Akums continues to revolutionize global healthcare by
providing high-quality, innovative pharmaceutical solutions with a patient-first approach,
strengthening its position as a driving force in the industry.

# 2026 Newsletter

We are grateful for the trust you place in us for your allergy and asthma care. At **Allergy &
Asthma Care, PA**, we are always striving to provide the best possible service while balancing the
needs of our patients and staff. Please review the following changes the practice will implement
next year.

Our confirmation platform will continue to be monitored through **Phreesia**. We request that
patients pre-register for their appointments, scan insurance cards, and verify demographic
information annually. It is important to confirm coverage information with your insurance plan, as
some HMO plans may no longer be in network or may require a referral from a primary care physician.

If you are changing insurance plans and are on a biologic or infused medication, please provide the
front and back of your insurance card as soon as possible. Our office will need to initiate new
prior authorizations, which may take additional time to process.

Beginning next year, we will send **electronic statements**. Please ensure we have your current
email address on file. Payments can be made through the Phreesia system, by calling the billing
department, or through our website.

Our Group

Established in 1977, Allergy & Asthma Care, P.A. is the oldest and largest continuously operating
allergy and asthma practice in metropolitan Kansas City. Our physicians are Board Certified in

# Our Mission

Our Board Certified allergists, associate providers, and staff are committed to providing the

# Our Vision

To be innovative leaders in the treatment of allergy, asthma, and immunology in our community and
surrounding areas. We are dedicated to working with the medical community in advancing the
importance of recognizing and treating allergic and immunologic diseases.

Patient education, cutting edge treatment, and a caring environment are pillars in our practice.
Continuing these core values attests to the commitment to our patients and our field.

[

## Allergies

Allergies are an abnormal response of the immune system in which the body’s defenses react to a
usually harmless substance in the environment (aeroallergen).

][68]
[Learn More][69]
[

## Asthma

Asthma is a chronic inflammatory disease of the airways found in individuals of any age. Asthma may
be chronic, ongoing, and quite severe or may be mild enough to only affect patients at certain times
or certain situations.

][70]
[Learn More][71]
[

## Sinus Conditions

The sinuses are open chambers within the head lined by a mucous membrane and function to lighten the
skull, making it easier for humans to walk upright.

][72]
[Learn More][73]
[

## Food Allergies

Food allergies are a common problem affecting about 3% of adults and about 7% of children. Food
allergies occur when a person’s immune system hyper-reacts to a specific food by producing specific
IgE antibodies.

][74]

surrounding areas. We are dedicated to working with the medical community in advancing the
importance of recognizing and treating allergic and immunologic diseases.

Patient education, cutting edge treatment, and a caring environment are pillars in our practice.
Continuing these core values attests to the commitment to our patients and our field.

[

## Allergies

Allergies are an abnormal response of the immune system in which the body’s defenses react to a
usually harmless substance in the environment (aeroallergen).

][68]
[Learn More][69]
[

## Asthma

Asthma is a chronic inflammatory disease of the airways found in individuals of any age. Asthma may
be chronic, ongoing, and quite severe or may be mild enough to only affect patients at certain times
or certain situations.

][70]
[Learn More][71]
[

## Sinus Conditions

The sinuses are open chambers within the head lined by a mucous membrane and function to lighten the
skull, making it easier for humans to walk upright.

][72]
[Learn More][73]
[

## Food Allergies

Food allergies are a common problem affecting about 3% of adults and about 7% of children. Food
allergies occur when a person’s immune system hyper-reacts to a specific food by producing specific
IgE antibodies.

][74]
[Learn More][75]

# MOVING IN UNISON

We work as a flexible, attentive extension of your team; we offer the contract research organization
services you need to move your molecule from preclinical to Phase I, Phase II, and beyond.

[ Contact Us ][14]

[play brand video ][15] [pause brand video ][16]
[5 Strategies to Reduce AI Hallucination in Clinical Research by Seong min Cho]

#### 5 Strategies to Reduce AI Hallucination in Clinical Research by Seong min Cho

Learn 5 practical strategies to reduce AI hallucination in clinical research to improve accuracy,
transparency, compliance, and decision-making.

[Read now! ][17]

[A Day in the Life of A Molecule]

#### A Day in the Life of A Molecule

Press play to meet Mike the Molecule—he’s got big dreams and a big journey ahead! Follow along as he
takes on every stage of drug development here at Altasciences.Science has never been this fun!

[Learn more! ][18]

[A Day in the Life of a Veterinary Scientist, Ophthalmology]

#### A Day in the Life of a Veterinary Scientist, Ophthalmology

Marianna Bacellar-Galdino has always loved scientific research, and after a particularly eye-opening
project in veterinary school, ophthalmology became the thread connecting all her scientific
interests—and eventually her whole career.

[Watch now! ][19]

We are a forward-thinking, mid-size early phase contract research organization, in Canada and the
U.S., offering biopharmaceutical companies of all sizes a proven, flexible approach to early drug
development, including preclinical safety testing, clinical pharmacology (Phase I to Phase II),
bioanalysis (preclinical to Phase IV), research services, and manufacturing and analytical services.

Focused on your success … always available and always looking ahead ... moving in unison to deliver
big impact with a personal touch.

## WHAT WE DO

We help you reach early phase drug development decision-making milestones sooner, improving speed
and ease from lead candidate selection to proof of concept, and beyond.
* [ [Preclinical Services] ][20]
  
  #### [ **ALTA**SCIENCES Preclinical Services ][21]
  
  Safety assessments for both small and large molecules
* [ [Clinical Services] ][22]
  
  #### [ **ALTA**SCIENCES Clinical Services ][23]
  
  Clinical pharmacology trials from first-in-human to end of Phase II
* [ [Manufacturing and Analytical Services] ][24]
  
  #### [ **ALTA**SCIENCES Manufacturing and Analytical Services ][25]
  
  From formulation development, Phase I through commercial manufacturing, and ICH stability testing
* [ [thumb] ][26]
  
  #### [ **ALTA**SCIENCES Bioanalysis Services ][27]
  
  Package or stand-alone. Preclinical, Phase I to Phase IV bioanalytical laboratories
* [ [research support services] ][28]
  
  #### [ **ALTA**SCIENCES Research Support Services ][29]
  
  Comprehensive CRO services to support clinical and preclinical studies

## HIGHLIGHTS

Learn 5 practical strategies to reduce AI hallucination in clinical research to improve accuracy,
transparency, compliance, and decision-making.

[Read now! ][17]

[A Day in the Life of A Molecule]

#### A Day in the Life of A Molecule

Press play to meet Mike the Molecule—he’s got big dreams and a big journey ahead! Follow along as he
takes on every stage of drug development here at Altasciences.Science has never been this fun!

[Learn more! ][18]

[A Day in the Life of a Veterinary Scientist, Ophthalmology]

#### A Day in the Life of a Veterinary Scientist, Ophthalmology

Marianna Bacellar-Galdino has always loved scientific research, and after a particularly eye-opening
project in veterinary school, ophthalmology became the thread connecting all her scientific
interests—and eventually her whole career.

[Watch now! ][19]

We are a forward-thinking, mid-size early phase contract research organization, in Canada and the
U.S., offering biopharmaceutical companies of all sizes a proven, flexible approach to early drug
development, including preclinical safety testing, clinical pharmacology (Phase I to Phase II),
bioanalysis (preclinical to Phase IV), research services, and manufacturing and analytical services.

Focused on your success … always available and always looking ahead ... moving in unison to deliver
big impact with a personal touch.

We help you reach early phase drug development decision-making milestones sooner, improving speed
and ease from lead candidate selection to proof of concept, and beyond.

## Our vision is to be a leading global rare disease company by acquiring, developing and
## commercialising medicines that transform the lives of patients & their families around the world.

## About

At Amryt Pharma, we look beyond the ordinary, unearthing scientific potential and delivering
medicines that may have the potential to change the lives of people with rare, debilitating
conditions. Through our in-depth knowledge and bold approach we combine the expertise and innovation
needed to help patients and their caregivers to access new treatments quickly and responsibly.

[READ MORE][89]

### [Amryt Compliance][90]
### [Aegerion Consent Decree][91]

## Advocacy

Amryt Pharma supports the aims and objectives of advocacy groups working across rare and
debilitating diseases to help patients and their families and carers.

[READ MORE][92]

## Join us

This is an exciting time for Amryt Pharma. We are a successful, thriving global company poised to
achieve unparalleled results. Our success is driven and defined by the inspiring people who embody
our values and wake up every day with the goal of changing lives of people with rare and
debilitating diseases.

[GET IN TOUCH][93]

## Our vision is to be a leading global rare disease company by acquiring, developing and
## commercialising medicines that transform the lives of patients & their families around the world.

## About

At Amryt Pharma, we look beyond the ordinary, unearthing scientific potential and delivering
medicines that may have the potential to change the lives of people with rare, debilitating
conditions. Through our in-depth knowledge and bold approach we combine the expertise and innovation
needed to help patients and their caregivers to access new treatments quickly and responsibly.

[READ MORE][89]

### [Amryt Compliance][90]
### [Aegerion Consent Decree][91]

## Advocacy

Amryt Pharma supports the aims and objectives of advocacy groups working across rare and
debilitating diseases to help patients and their families and carers.

[READ MORE][92]

## Join us

This is an exciting time for Amryt Pharma. We are a successful, thriving global company poised to
achieve unparalleled results. Our success is driven and defined by the inspiring people who embody
our values and wake up every day with the goal of changing lives of people with rare and
debilitating diseases.

[GET IN TOUCH][93]

## Follow us and keep up to date

[2021 annual report][95]

## [Register for updates][96]

the site. If you have already subscribed you can also log-in through the link.

## Share price

We transform the lives of people affected by rare, debilitating conditions by providing innovative
medicines that bring hope to those in greatest need.

В Amsalem Medical Center мы глубоко понимаем ваши страхи, тревоги и ожидания, и именно поэтому
создаём индивидуальные программы, которые максимально точно отвечают вашим потребностям и дают
реальные результаты.

#### Для тех, кто борется с тяжёлыми
#### и редкими диагнозами

[Для тех, кто борется с тяжёлыми и редкими диагнозами]
**Вы столкнулись с серьёзным заболеванием и ищете надёжного партнёра в борьбе за жизнь.**
* **Персональный медицинский координатор** - ваш постоянный помощник и защитник, который будет
  сопровождать вас на каждом этапе лечения, обеспечивая внимание и поддержку.
* **Доступ к ведущим израильским специалистам**, обладающим богатым опытом работы с редкими и
  сложными случаями, применяющим инновационные методы лечения.

# UNLEASHING THE PROMISE OF T-CELL THERAPIES.

[ DISCOVER ATARA ][44]

## Cutting-edge science. A fresh approach.

Atara is an allogeneic T-cell immunotherapy company. We're harnessing the natural biology of T
cells—our body’s most effective weapon in fighting disease—to develop transformative therapies for
patients with cancer and autoimmune conditions.
* #### Off-the-shelf approach
  
  Allogeneic T-cell therapies can be readily available for rapid delivery within days.
* #### Scalable manufacturing
  
  Efficient, robust process with the ability to produce over a thousand doses from one healthy
  donor.
* #### Highly versatile platform
  
  Potential application for a wide range of disease-causing viral and non-viral targets.
[OUR TECHNOLOGY][45]

## We’re developing a pipeline of firsts.

Our investigational T-cell therapies target difficult-to-treat cancers and autoimmune conditions
that can be rapidly delivered to patients from inventory. We’re the first company ever to receive an
approval for an allogeneic T-cell immunotherapy.

# UNLEASHING THE PROMISE OF T-CELL THERAPIES.

[ DISCOVER ATARA ][44]

## Cutting-edge science. A fresh approach.

Atara is an allogeneic T-cell immunotherapy company. We're harnessing the natural biology of T
cells—our body’s most effective weapon in fighting disease—to develop transformative therapies for
patients with cancer and autoimmune conditions.
* #### Off-the-shelf approach
  
  Allogeneic T-cell therapies can be readily available for rapid delivery within days.
* #### Scalable manufacturing
  
  Efficient, robust process with the ability to produce over a thousand doses from one healthy
  donor.
* #### Highly versatile platform
  
  Potential application for a wide range of disease-causing viral and non-viral targets.
[OUR TECHNOLOGY][45]

## We’re developing a pipeline of firsts.

Our investigational T-cell therapies target difficult-to-treat cancers and autoimmune conditions
that can be rapidly delivered to patients from inventory. We’re the first company ever to receive an
approval for an allogeneic T-cell immunotherapy.

### CARBOGEN AMCIS Commissions Ground-Mounted Pho-tovoltaic Plant at Its Hunzenschwil Site

CARBOGEN AMCIS, a Switzerland-based pharmaceutical process development and Active Pharmaceutical
Ingredient (API) manufacturing company, has suc-cessfully commissioned a new ground-mounted
photovoltaic system at its Hunzenschwil site in Switzerland. With this project, the company
underscores its long-term commitment to sustainability and the expansion of renewable energy.

## 1. Introduction to Clinical Studies

Clinical studies, often referred to as **clinical trials**, form the backbone of evidence-based
medicine. These are carefully designed research investigations involving human participants, aimed
at evaluating the safety and efficacy of drugs, medical devices, or other health interventions.
Clinical research provides crucial data that informs *regulatory decisions*, prescribing guidelines,
and public health policies.

There are two main types of clinical studies: **interventional studies**, where researchers assign
participants to receive specific treatments, and **observational studies**, where outcomes are
observed without intervention. The term “clinical trial” typically refers to interventional studies,
especially those that test new drugs or therapies in a phased manner.

Without clinical trials, there would be no safe vaccines, no proven cancer therapies, and no
effective diagnostics. Whether sponsored by pharmaceutical companies, governments, academic
institutions, or non-profits, *clinical studies advance medical science* and improve patient care
globally.

Understanding the structure, process, and stakeholders involved in clinical research is critical for
professionals and participants alike. This guide provides a comprehensive look into the journey of
clinical studies, from protocol design to patient care improvements.

## 2. Objectives and Phases of Clinical Trials

The **primary objective of clinical trials** is to answer specific research questions related to new
medical products or interventions. These may include questions about safety, dosage, efficacy, side
effects, or comparative effectiveness with existing treatments. Every clinical trial is built around
a hypothesis and a protocol that defines how the study will be conducted.

Clinical trials are typically divided into four distinct phases, each serving a unique purpose in
the *drug development lifecycle*:

### Phase 0 (Microdosing Studies)

Conducted on a very small number of participants, Phase 0 trials test sub-therapeutic doses of a
drug to understand pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics.

### Phase I (Safety and Tolerability)

This phase involves 20–100 healthy volunteers or patients and focuses on **safety, dosage range, and
side effects**. Phase I is often conducted in specialized clinical pharmacology units under strict
monitoring.

### Phase II (Efficacy and Side Effects)

Involving 100–300 participants, this phase explores whether the drug works as intended. It continues
safety evaluation and helps refine dosing protocols.

### Phase III (Confirmatory Trials)

Large-scale trials involving 1,000–3,000 participants, often across multiple sites and countries.
The data from Phase III is used for *regulatory submissions to agencies like the FDA or EMA*.

### Phase IV (Post-Marketing Surveillance)

Once a drug is approved, Phase IV trials monitor its performance in the general population and
identify any long-term effects or rare adverse reactions.

Each phase builds upon the previous one, and only a small percentage of drugs progress from early to
late-stage trials. Understanding these phases is essential for **GCP compliance**, ethical
oversight, and informed decision-making.

## 3. Types of Clinical Studies

Clinical research is not limited to testing new drugs. The methodologies vary depending on the study
objectives and endpoints. Below are some of the most common types of clinical studies:

### Interventional Studies

Participants are assigned to receive a specific treatment, and researchers observe outcomes based on
predefined endpoints. Examples include trials testing new drugs, vaccines, surgical techniques, or
behavioral interventions.

### Observational Studies

Researchers observe and analyze health outcomes without assigning interventions. These may include
**cohort studies**, **case-control studies**, or **cross-sectional analyses**.

### Randomized Controlled Trials (RCTs)

RCTs are the gold standard in clinical research. Participants are randomly assigned to treatment or
control groups to minimize bias and provide statistically valid results.

### Adaptive Trials

Designed to allow modifications to the protocol mid-study based on interim analysis. These are
increasingly used in oncology and rare disease trials.

### Pragmatic Trials

These trials evaluate interventions under real-world clinical conditions and are useful for
assessing effectiveness in everyday healthcare settings.

### Real-World Evidence (RWE) Studies

These studies utilize *real-world data* (RWD) from electronic health records, claims databases, or
patient registries to evaluate treatment outcomes outside controlled trial environments.

Each type of study offers unique insights and is chosen based on the medical question, ethical
considerations, and regulatory pathways involved.

## 4. Stakeholders in Clinical Trials

The successful conduct of a clinical trial depends on a wide network of **stakeholders**, each
playing a unique and vital role. Understanding who these players are helps in appreciating the
complexity and coordination required in clinical research.

### Sponsors

Sponsors are individuals, companies, institutions, or organizations that initiate and fund the
clinical study. Pharmaceutical companies, biotech firms, and academic research centers often act as
sponsors. Their responsibilities include protocol development, regulatory submissions, site
selection, and oversight of the trial’s execution.

### Contract Research Organizations (CROs)

CROs are hired by sponsors to manage specific aspects of the trial such as monitoring, data
management, statistical analysis, or even full project execution. They serve as an operational arm
to increase efficiency, especially in multinational trials.

### Principal Investigators (PIs)

PIs are licensed medical doctors responsible for conducting the study at individual sites. They
ensure adherence to *GCP guidelines*, supervise the research team, and maintain data integrity.

### Ethics Committees / IRBs

Institutional Review Boards (IRBs) or Ethics Committees (ECs) review and approve the study protocol,
consent forms, and study amendments. Their core role is to protect the rights and safety of human
subjects.

### Regulatory Authorities

Agencies like the US FDA, EMA, CDSCO (India), PMDA (Japan), and others regulate the initiation and
conduct of clinical trials. They review applications, grant approvals, and conduct inspections to
ensure ethical and scientific compliance.

### Patients and Advocacy Groups

Patients are at the center of every clinical trial. Their willingness to participate drives medical
innovation. Advocacy groups also play an important role by improving awareness, recruitment, and
engagement for specific disease areas.

Collaboration among these stakeholders is crucial for a successful trial outcome and for ensuring
**participant safety, data quality, and regulatory compliance**.

## 5. Clinical Trial Process Step-by-Step

Every clinical trial follows a carefully defined process, beginning long before the first
participant is enrolled and continuing through data analysis and publication. Here’s a high-level
overview:

### Step 1: Protocol Development

The sponsor drafts a protocol that outlines the study objectives, inclusion/exclusion criteria,
dosing, monitoring, endpoints, and statistical methods.

### Step 2: Regulatory and Ethics Approvals

Submissions are made to health authorities (e.g., FDA, EMA) and IRBs/ECs for approval. Approval is
required before any patient activity begins.

### Step 3: Site Selection and Initiation

Sites with relevant experience and infrastructure are selected. Site initiation visits are
conducted, and training is provided on protocol, safety, and systems.

### Step 4: Patient Recruitment and Informed Consent

Eligible patients are identified and given detailed information about the study. Participation is
voluntary, and informed consent is documented before any procedures.

### Step 5: Study Conduct and Monitoring

Patients receive the investigational product or intervention, and data is collected at each visit.
CRAs monitor the site for GCP compliance and data accuracy.

### Step 6: Data Analysis and Submission

Data is cleaned, coded, and analyzed by statisticians. Results are submitted to regulatory bodies
and often published in scientific journals.

### Step 7: Study Close-Out

Sites are closed, regulatory documents archived, and results shared. If successful, the intervention
may move into regulatory approval and commercialization.

Each step involves meticulous documentation and coordination between sponsors, investigators, CROs,
and regulators to ensure trial validity and *ethical compliance*.

## 6. Patient Participation and Rights

Clinical trial participants are more than subjects — they are partners in the advancement of
medicine. Ensuring **ethical treatment, informed decision-making, and safety** is a cornerstone of
clinical research.

### Why Patients Participate
* Access to cutting-edge treatments not available outside the trial
* Better medical care and frequent monitoring
* Altruistic desire to help advance science

### Informed Consent Process

Before joining a study, patients must be informed of the risks, benefits, procedures, alternatives,
and their rights. This process includes a written consent form and verbal discussions with study
staff. Patients can withdraw at any time without losing access to care.

# Clinical Studies Explained: From Research to Real-World Impact

# Understanding Clinical Studies: From Concept to Cure

Table of Contents

[Toggle][43]
* [1. Introduction to Clinical Studies][44]
* [2. Objectives and Phases of Clinical Trials][45]
* [3. Types of Clinical Studies][46]
* [4. Stakeholders in Clinical Trials][47]
* [5. Clinical Trial Process Step-by-Step][48]
* [6. Patient Participation and Rights][49]
* [7. Global Regulations and Guidelines][50]
* [8. Challenges in Clinical Trials][51]
* [9. Innovations Transforming Clinical Research][52]
* [10. The Future of Clinical Trials][53]
* [11. ClinicalStudies.in: Your Guide to Global Clinical Research][54]

## 1. Introduction to Clinical Studies

Clinical studies, often referred to as **clinical trials**, form the backbone of evidence-based
medicine. These are carefully designed research investigations involving human participants, aimed
at evaluating the safety and efficacy of drugs, medical devices, or other health interventions.
Clinical research provides crucial data that informs *regulatory decisions*, prescribing guidelines,
and public health policies.

There are two main types of clinical studies: **interventional studies**, where researchers assign
participants to receive specific treatments, and **observational studies**, where outcomes are
observed without intervention. The term “clinical trial” typically refers to interventional studies,
especially those that test new drugs or therapies in a phased manner.

Without clinical trials, there would be no safe vaccines, no proven cancer therapies, and no
effective diagnostics. Whether sponsored by pharmaceutical companies, governments, academic
institutions, or non-profits, *clinical studies advance medical science* and improve patient care
globally.

Understanding the structure, process, and stakeholders involved in clinical research is critical for
professionals and participants alike. This guide provides a comprehensive look into the journey of
clinical studies, from protocol design to patient care improvements.

## 2. Objectives and Phases of Clinical Trials

The **primary objective of clinical trials** is to answer specific research questions related to new
medical products or interventions. These may include questions about safety, dosage, efficacy, side
effects, or comparative effectiveness with existing treatments. Every clinical trial is built around
a hypothesis and a protocol that defines how the study will be conducted.

Clinical trials are typically divided into four distinct phases, each serving a unique purpose in
the *drug development lifecycle*:

### Phase 0 (Microdosing Studies)

Conducted on a very small number of participants, Phase 0 trials test sub-therapeutic doses of a
drug to understand pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics.

### Phase I (Safety and Tolerability)

This phase involves 20–100 healthy volunteers or patients and focuses on **safety, dosage range, and
side effects**. Phase I is often conducted in specialized clinical pharmacology units under strict
monitoring.

### Phase II (Efficacy and Side Effects)

Involving 100–300 participants, this phase explores whether the drug works as intended. It continues
safety evaluation and helps refine dosing protocols.

### Phase III (Confirmatory Trials)

Large-scale trials involving 1,000–3,000 participants, often across multiple sites and countries.
The data from Phase III is used for *regulatory submissions to agencies like the FDA or EMA*.

### Phase IV (Post-Marketing Surveillance)

Once a drug is approved, Phase IV trials monitor its performance in the general population and
identify any long-term effects or rare adverse reactions.

Each phase builds upon the previous one, and only a small percentage of drugs progress from early to
late-stage trials. Understanding these phases is essential for **GCP compliance**, ethical
oversight, and informed decision-making.

## 3. Types of Clinical Studies

Clinical research is not limited to testing new drugs. The methodologies vary depending on the study
objectives and endpoints. Below are some of the most common types of clinical studies:

### Interventional Studies

Participants are assigned to receive a specific treatment, and researchers observe outcomes based on
predefined endpoints. Examples include trials testing new drugs, vaccines, surgical techniques, or
behavioral interventions.

### Observational Studies

Researchers observe and analyze health outcomes without assigning interventions. These may include
**cohort studies**, **case-control studies**, or **cross-sectional analyses**.

### Randomized Controlled Trials (RCTs)

RCTs are the gold standard in clinical research. Participants are randomly assigned to treatment or
control groups to minimize bias and provide statistically valid results.

### Adaptive Trials

Designed to allow modifications to the protocol mid-study based on interim analysis. These are
increasingly used in oncology and rare disease trials.

### Pragmatic Trials

These trials evaluate interventions under real-world clinical conditions and are useful for
assessing effectiveness in everyday healthcare settings.

### Real-World Evidence (RWE) Studies

These studies utilize *real-world data* (RWD) from electronic health records, claims databases, or
patient registries to evaluate treatment outcomes outside controlled trial environments.

Each type of study offers unique insights and is chosen based on the medical question, ethical
considerations, and regulatory pathways involved.

## 4. Stakeholders in Clinical Trials

The successful conduct of a clinical trial depends on a wide network of **stakeholders**, each
playing a unique and vital role. Understanding who these players are helps in appreciating the
complexity and coordination required in clinical research.

### Sponsors

Sponsors are individuals, companies, institutions, or organizations that initiate and fund the
clinical study. Pharmaceutical companies, biotech firms, and academic research centers often act as
sponsors. Their responsibilities include protocol development, regulatory submissions, site
selection, and oversight of the trial’s execution.

### Contract Research Organizations (CROs)

CROs are hired by sponsors to manage specific aspects of the trial such as monitoring, data
management, statistical analysis, or even full project execution. They serve as an operational arm
to increase efficiency, especially in multinational trials.

### Principal Investigators (PIs)

PIs are licensed medical doctors responsible for conducting the study at individual sites. They
ensure adherence to *GCP guidelines*, supervise the research team, and maintain data integrity.

### Ethics Committees / IRBs

Institutional Review Boards (IRBs) or Ethics Committees (ECs) review and approve the study protocol,
consent forms, and study amendments. Their core role is to protect the rights and safety of human
subjects.

### Regulatory Authorities

Agencies like the US FDA, EMA, CDSCO (India), PMDA (Japan), and others regulate the initiation and
conduct of clinical trials. They review applications, grant approvals, and conduct inspections to
ensure ethical and scientific compliance.

### Patients and Advocacy Groups

Patients are at the center of every clinical trial. Their willingness to participate drives medical
innovation. Advocacy groups also play an important role by improving awareness, recruitment, and
engagement for specific disease areas.

Collaboration among these stakeholders is crucial for a successful trial outcome and for ensuring
**participant safety, data quality, and regulatory compliance**.

## 5. Clinical Trial Process Step-by-Step

Every clinical trial follows a carefully defined process, beginning long before the first
participant is enrolled and continuing through data analysis and publication. Here’s a high-level
overview:

### Step 1: Protocol Development

The sponsor drafts a protocol that outlines the study objectives, inclusion/exclusion criteria,
dosing, monitoring, endpoints, and statistical methods.

### Step 2: Regulatory and Ethics Approvals

Submissions are made to health authorities (e.g., FDA, EMA) and IRBs/ECs for approval. Approval is
required before any patient activity begins.

### Step 3: Site Selection and Initiation

Sites with relevant experience and infrastructure are selected. Site initiation visits are
conducted, and training is provided on protocol, safety, and systems.

### Step 4: Patient Recruitment and Informed Consent

Eligible patients are identified and given detailed information about the study. Participation is
voluntary, and informed consent is documented before any procedures.

### Step 5: Study Conduct and Monitoring

Patients receive the investigational product or intervention, and data is collected at each visit.
CRAs monitor the site for GCP compliance and data accuracy.

### Step 6: Data Analysis and Submission

Data is cleaned, coded, and analyzed by statisticians. Results are submitted to regulatory bodies
and often published in scientific journals.

### Step 7: Study Close-Out

Sites are closed, regulatory documents archived, and results shared. If successful, the intervention
may move into regulatory approval and commercialization.

Each step involves meticulous documentation and coordination between sponsors, investigators, CROs,
and regulators to ensure trial validity and *ethical compliance*.

## 6. Patient Participation and Rights

Clinical trial participants are more than subjects — they are partners in the advancement of
medicine. Ensuring **ethical treatment, informed decision-making, and safety** is a cornerstone of
clinical research.

### Why Patients Participate
* Access to cutting-edge treatments not available outside the trial
* Better medical care and frequent monitoring
* Altruistic desire to help advance science

### Informed Consent Process

Before joining a study, patients must be informed of the risks, benefits, procedures, alternatives,
and their rights. This process includes a written consent form and verbal discussions with study
staff. Patients can withdraw at any time without losing access to care.

Our commitment to affordability is unwavering. We leverage long-standing manufacturer partnerships

our promise of compliance, reliability, and consistent quality—helping healthcare providers maintain
cost efficiency without compromise.


#### Commitment to Innovation

By investing in advanced technology, Drugzone streamlines ordering, tracking, and compliance.
Healthcare partners—from specialty clinics to hospital chains—benefit from secure, efficient, and
transparent operations. Our integrated ERP and compliance monitoring systems enhance real-time
visibility, inventory accuracy, and traceability throughout the supply chain.


#### Partner-Centric Approach

Long-term relationships drive our success. Drugzone works closely with hospitals, LTC providers, and
specialty networks—listening to their needs and delivering solutions that help them serve their
patients better. Our dedicated account managers provide personalized support, ensuring every partner
experiences responsive communication, consistent supply, and measurable value from our
collaboration.

## Comprehensive Distribution Capabilities

Drugzone combines industry expertise with strong logistics to provide comprehensive generic
distribution services. Each capability is designed to help healthcare and specialty partners
maintain a safe, seamless, and cost-effective supply chain.

### Wholesale& Specialty Distribution

Reliable, nationwide generic pharmaceutical supply for healthcare and specialty care providers
across the U.S. Our consistent processes make us a trusted choice among wholesale pharmaceutical
distributors in the U.S.

### Logistics& Warehousing

State-of-the-art warehouses and a nationwide delivery network ensure secure storage and timely
shipments, reducing inventory gaps for healthcare networks nationwide.

### Provider& Pharmacy Solutions

and maintain an uninterrupted treatment supply.

### Compliance& Quality Assurance

checks to ensure healthcare providers—across human and animal health—receive authentic and traceable
products.

Drugzone strengthens its nationwide supply reliability through long-standing partnerships with
leading generic manufacturers. These strategic alliances ensure verified authenticity, stable
pricing, and consistent access to essential medications across multiple therapeutic areas.

reliable access to quality pharmaceuticals across the U.S. under NABP, FDA, and DSCSA 2025

formulations. Each product is stored and distributed following the strictest compliance standards.

## Mission & Vision

[img]

### Mission

To advance healthcare delivery by ensuring access to safe, effective, and affordable generic
pharmaceuticals through innovation, compliance, and service excellence. Drugzone is committed to
empowering healthcare providers—hospitals, long-term care facilities, specialty clinics, and
veterinary networks—through transparent operations, ethical sourcing, and nationwide reliability.
* **Our mission focuses on:**
* Ensuring secure, compliant, and traceable pharmaceutical distribution across all 50 states.
* Maintaining ethical and transparent partnerships with healthcare providers and manufacturers.
* Promoting innovation in logistics, compliance, and digital fulfillment for greater efficiency.
* Upholding regulatory integrity through NABP, FDA, and DSCSA 2025 compliance.
* Creating long-term value by prioritizing patient safety and partner trust.

[img]

### Vision

To be among the nation’s most trusted pharmaceutical distribution companies, defined by integrity,
professionalism, and continuous innovation. Drugzone envisions a future where compliant and
affordable access to quality pharmaceuticals strengthens the entire continuum of care.
* **Our vision aspires to:**
* Lead the U.S. market as a benchmark in generic pharmaceutical distribution.
* Advance technology-driven operations that enhance fulfillment speed and traceability.
* Build sustainable business practices that support healthcare accessibility nationwide.
* Foster a partner-first culture rooted in transparency and responsiveness.
* Continue setting new standards of reliability and trust across human and animal health sectors.

# Funding European Diabetes Research

**Our foundation encourages and supports groundbreaking diabetes research and promotes the next
generation of leading scientists**

The following grant or fellowship programmes are currently open for applications:

##### EFSD & Japan Diabetes Society Reciprocal Travel Research Fellowship Programme

Encouraging collaborative research for scientists or clinicians working in a postdoctoral position
in the field of diabetes.

**Application deadline: 27 July 2026**

[Learn more][124]

##### EFSD and Lilly European Diabetes Research Programme**
##### **

Promoting increased European diabetes research, raising public awareness and political understanding
of the magnitude and burden of the disease.

**Application deadline: 1 September 2026**

[**Learn more**][125]

## EASD e-learning

New on EASD e-Learning

#### [Have your say!][126]

EASD Guideline on the use of continuous glucose monitoring for the management of type 2 diabetes

#### [AID in older people, even with cognitive deficits?][127]

Should age really decide who is “fit” for automated insulin delivery?

#### [Long-acting amylins][128]

A novel therapeutic mechanism and what we know about it

#### [Why not to use LLMs for carb counting & insulin dosing yet][129]

From training data to reliability

## Podcasts

Tune in to Diabetes Insights

#### [Harvesting the Seeds from Funding Type 1 Diabetes Research][130]

In this episode, Elizabeth Robertson (Diabetes UK) and Rachel Connor (Breakthrough T1D) discuss one
of the most exciting developments in diabetes research: the growing possibility of delaying and
ultimately preventing type 1 diabetes.

#### [Challenges and Opportunities - How EASD Turned Global][131]

In this episode, former EASD President Prof. Stefano Del Prato joins EASD TV host Vivienne Parry to
reflect on leading EASD during the unprecedented challenges of the COVID-19 pandemic.

#### [AI in Diabetes Care][132]

In this episode, Prof. Joao Filipe Raposo (Sociedade Portuguesa de Diabetologia) and Prof. Harald
Sourij (Österreichische Diabetes Gesellschaft) join Vivienne Parry to debate one of the most
discussed topics in modern diabetes care: the role of artificial intelligence.

#### [Global Collaboration: East - West Exchange to Learn from Each Other][133]

In this episode, EASD tv host Vivienne Parry speaks with Prof. Daisuke Yabe about the growing global
impact of EASD and the importance of international collaboration in diabetes research.

# Submit to our Journals

**Publish your research in Diabetologia and Metabologia**

EASD has two journals, [**Diabetologia**][134], which publishes articles on all aspects of diabetes,
from basic science through translational work to clinical research, and [**Metabologia**][135], an
open access journal for research across the fields of diabetes, obesity, metabolism and related

#### [EASD-Novo Nordisk Prize for Excellence][122]

Join us in celebrating Prof. Kei Sakamoto, 2026 EASD-Novo Nordisk Foundation Prize for Excellence
recipient, awarded for his outstanding achievements in research which has led to significant
advances in the understanding, prevention or treatment of diabetes or its complications.

[Learn more][123]

# Funding European Diabetes Research

**Our foundation encourages and supports groundbreaking diabetes research and promotes the next
generation of leading scientists**

The following grant or fellowship programmes are currently open for applications:

##### EFSD & Japan Diabetes Society Reciprocal Travel Research Fellowship Programme

Encouraging collaborative research for scientists or clinicians working in a postdoctoral position
in the field of diabetes.

**Application deadline: 27 July 2026**

[Learn more][124]

##### EFSD and Lilly European Diabetes Research Programme**
##### **

Promoting increased European diabetes research, raising public awareness and political understanding
of the magnitude and burden of the disease.

**Application deadline: 1 September 2026**

[**Learn more**][125]

## EASD e-learning

New on EASD e-Learning

#### [Have your say!][126]

EASD Guideline on the use of continuous glucose monitoring for the management of type 2 diabetes

#### [AID in older people, even with cognitive deficits?][127]

Should age really decide who is “fit” for automated insulin delivery?

#### [Long-acting amylins][128]

A novel therapeutic mechanism and what we know about it

#### [Why not to use LLMs for carb counting & insulin dosing yet][129]

From training data to reliability

## Podcasts

Tune in to Diabetes Insights

#### [Harvesting the Seeds from Funding Type 1 Diabetes Research][130]

In this episode, Elizabeth Robertson (Diabetes UK) and Rachel Connor (Breakthrough T1D) discuss one
of the most exciting developments in diabetes research: the growing possibility of delaying and
ultimately preventing type 1 diabetes.

#### [Challenges and Opportunities - How EASD Turned Global][131]

In this episode, former EASD President Prof. Stefano Del Prato joins EASD TV host Vivienne Parry to
reflect on leading EASD during the unprecedented challenges of the COVID-19 pandemic.

#### [AI in Diabetes Care][132]

In this episode, Prof. Joao Filipe Raposo (Sociedade Portuguesa de Diabetologia) and Prof. Harald
Sourij (Österreichische Diabetes Gesellschaft) join Vivienne Parry to debate one of the most
discussed topics in modern diabetes care: the role of artificial intelligence.

#### [Global Collaboration: East - West Exchange to Learn from Each Other][133]

In this episode, EASD tv host Vivienne Parry speaks with Prof. Daisuke Yabe about the growing global
impact of EASD and the importance of international collaboration in diabetes research.

# Submit to our Journals

**Publish your research in Diabetologia and Metabologia**

EASD has two journals, [**Diabetologia**][134], which publishes articles on all aspects of diabetes,
from basic science through translational work to clinical research, and [**Metabologia**][135], an
open access journal for research across the fields of diabetes, obesity, metabolism and related
disorders. Both offer a platform for original studies, clinical trials, reviews, and
interdisciplinary work that inform scientific understanding and clinical practice.

* 12
  CiteScore
  CiteScore measures the average citations received per peer-reviewed document. CiteScore values are
  based on citation counts in a range of four years to peer-reviewed documents published in the same
  four calendar years, divided by the number of these documents in these same four years.
  2025 CiteScore © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

## About

### ESMO Open

[[Cover Image - ESMO Open, Volume 11, Issue 7]][78]

*ESMO Open* is the European Society for Medical Oncology's online-only, peer-reviewed open access
journal, dedicated to publishing high-quality medical research and educational content from all
disciplines of oncology, with a focus on innovative clinical and translational cancer research. The
Journal aims to maximize industry networks to curate and disseminate preclinical or translational
data. We hope to bridge the gap between basic research and clinical applications, facilitating the
translation of groundbreaking discoveries into tangible advancements in cancer care. Our platform
will serve as a catalyst for innovation, nurturing the dialogue between academia, industry, and
clinical practice.

### ESMO

[ESMO  Opens in new window][79]   is the European Society for Medical Oncology. Representing over
50,000 members globally, ESMO is a reference for oncology education and information.

Founded in 1975, ESMO has European roots with a global reach. Home for all oncology stakeholders,
ESMO connects professionals with diverse expertise and experience. Its education and information
resources support an integrated multi-professional approach to cancer care, from a medical oncology
perspective.

ESMO seeks to erase boundaries in cancer care, whether between countries or specialities, and pursue
its mission across oncology, worldwide.

[ESMO Guidelines Opens in new window][80]

## About

### ESMO Open

[[Cover Image - ESMO Open, Volume 11, Issue 7]][78]

*ESMO Open* is the European Society for Medical Oncology's online-only, peer-reviewed open access
journal, dedicated to publishing high-quality medical research and educational content from all
disciplines of oncology, with a focus on innovative clinical and translational cancer research. The
Journal aims to maximize industry networks to curate and disseminate preclinical or translational
data. We hope to bridge the gap between basic research and clinical applications, facilitating the
translation of groundbreaking discoveries into tangible advancements in cancer care. Our platform
will serve as a catalyst for innovation, nurturing the dialogue between academia, industry, and
clinical practice.

### ESMO

[ESMO  Opens in new window][79]   is the European Society for Medical Oncology. Representing over
50,000 members globally, ESMO is a reference for oncology education and information.

Founded in 1975, ESMO has European roots with a global reach. Home for all oncology stakeholders,
ESMO connects professionals with diverse expertise and experience. Its education and information
resources support an integrated multi-professional approach to cancer care, from a medical oncology
perspective.

ESMO seeks to erase boundaries in cancer care, whether between countries or specialities, and pursue
its mission across oncology, worldwide.

[ESMO Guidelines Opens in new window][80]

About Us

## World's #1 Paracetamol API Manufacturer with 50+ Years of Excellence

For over 50 years, Farmson Basic Drugs has been India's most trusted GMP-certified API
pharmaceutical manufacturer. As the world's largest Paracetamol API producer, we supply
acetaminophen and other pharmaceutical APIs to 400+ partners across 65+ countries.

Farmson was established in the year 1969 for manufacturing of Paracetamol through phenol route. In
the year 2000, we switched over to the PNCB route to manufacture Paracetamol. Currently, we are the
GLOBAL LEADER in API Paracetamol production.

With the motto of self-reliance, in 2005, we set up a plant in Jhagadia-Bharuch with backward
integration for manufacturing of PAP from PNCB wherein we were the first and only company producing
PAP through Hydrogenation process. For manufacturing API Paracetamol, we commissioned Unit-II in
2012, while in 2018, Unit-I was renovated & restructured to further expand our capacity.
